notes.md: - **Later use:** The **Chola** bronzes of South India, such as the **Nataraja**, were also cast by the **lost-wax** method.

new.s: In which district of Gujarat is Dholavira located?
new.x: Dholavira lies in Kachchh district of Gujarat.
new.angle: U0007 notes gap: Dholavira -> Kachchh

new.s: At which Harappan site have ornamental bricks been found?
new.x: Ornamental bricks come from Kalibangan; curved bricks are from Chanhudaro.
new.angle: U0007 notes gap: ornamental bricks -> Kalibangan

new.s: At which site has the early pottery of the Indus region been found?
new.x: Early pottery of the region is found at Mehrgarh in Balochistan.
new.angle: U0007 notes gap: early pottery -> Mehrgarh

new.s: At which site were wheat and barley found in a wooden mortar?
new.x: Wheat and barley in a wooden mortar are among the finds at Harappa.
new.angle: U0007 notes gap: wooden mortar with wheat and barley -> Harappa

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five largest Harappan cities?
new.x: The five largest are Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi and Dholavira; Lothal was a small port town.
new.angle: U0007 notes gap: five largest cities

new.s: Who discovered Dholavira in 1967-68?
new.x: J.P. Joshi found Dholavira in 1967-68; R.S. Bisht later led the large excavation.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Dholavira -> J.P. Joshi (found)

new.s: Which archaeologist excavated both Banawali and Dholavira?
new.x: R.S. Bisht dug Banawali (1973-74) and led the large dig at Dholavira.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: R.S. Bisht -> Banawali and Dholavira

new.s: Who among the following first excavated Rakhigarhi for the ASI?
new.x: Rakhigarhi was excavated by Amarendra Nath of the ASI (1997); Vasant Shinde dug it later.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Rakhigarhi -> Amarendra Nath / Vasant Shinde

new.s: Who first excavated Rangpur in 1931?
new.x: M.S. Vats dug Rangpur in 1931; S.R. Rao dug it again in 1953-54.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Rangpur -> M.S. Vats

new.s: Who excavated Ropar, the first Harappan site dug after Independence?
new.x: Ropar was excavated by Y.D. Sharma in 1955-56.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Ropar -> Y.D. Sharma

new.s: On the bank of which river is Mohenjodaro situated?
new.x: Mohenjodaro stands on the Indus in Larkana district of Sindh.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Mohenjodaro -> Indus

new.s: On which river is Lothal located?
new.x: Lothal in Ahmedabad district lies on the Bhogava (Sabarmati area).
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Lothal -> Bhogava

new.s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (River):
List-I
A. Kalibangan
B. Rangpur
C. Ropar
List-II
1. Sutlej
2. Sukhbhadar
3. Ghaggar
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Kalibangan is on the Ghaggar, Rangpur on the Sukhbhadar and Ropar on the Sutlej.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Kalibangan -> Ghaggar, Rangpur -> Sukhbhadar

new.s: On which island in the Rann of Kachchh is Dholavira situated?
new.x: Dholavira lies on Khadir island in the Rann of Kachchh.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Dholavira -> Khadir island

new.s: At which Harappan site have camel bones been found?
new.x: Camel bones are reported from Kalibangan, along with the ploughed field and fire altars.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: camel bones -> Kalibangan

new.s: At which site was a terracotta toy plough found?
new.x: The toy (terracotta) plough comes from Banawali; the ploughed field is at Kalibangan.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: toy plough -> Banawali

new.s: At which Harappan site was an inkpot found?
new.x: Chanhudaro, the bead-making town, also yielded an inkpot.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: inkpot -> Chanhudaro

new.s: Which Gujarat site, known for rice husks, belongs to the Late Harappan (Rojdi culture) phase?
new.x: Rangpur yielded rice husks and belongs to the Late Harappan (Rojdi culture) phase.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Rangpur -> Late Harappan, Rojdi

new.s: In which year was Mohenjodaro inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
new.x: Mohenjodaro (Pakistan) was inscribed in 1980; Dholavira in India followed in 2021.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Mohenjodaro UNESCO 1980

new.s: Which Union Ministry is developing the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal?
o: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
new.x: The NMHC at Lothal is a project of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: NMHC -> Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC):
1. It is being developed at Lothal in Gujarat.
2. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NMHC at Lothal was approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2024.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: NMHC approved Oct 2024

new.s: How many complete skeletons were found in the Rakhigarhi excavation reported in June 2026?
new.x: The June 2026 dig found five complete skeletons (aged 30-40) and three fragmentary burials.
new.angle: U0008 notes gap: Rakhigarhi June 2026 dig

new.s: With which early development is Kili Gul Muhammad (c. 4000 BC) associated?
new.x: Kili Gul Muhammad gives early evidence of animal domestication and agriculture, c. 4000 BC.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: Kili Gul Muhammad

new.s: Where has the earliest evidence of iron in India been found?
new.x: The earliest iron in India is from Atranjikhera on the Kali river, dug by R.C. Gaur in 1962.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: earliest iron -> Atranjikhera

new.s: At which Harappan site has evidence of cotton been found?
new.x: Cotton evidence comes from Mohenjodaro (and Mehrgarh); the Harappans first grew cotton.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: cotton -> Mohenjodaro

new.s: Which crop, unknown to the Harappans, was brought to India by the Portuguese?
new.x: Maize came to India with the Portuguese; it was unknown in India before.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: maize -> Portuguese

new.s: At which site were copper figures of a rhinoceros and an elephant found?
new.x: Copper rhinoceros and elephant figures come from Daimabad.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: copper rhino and elephant -> Daimabad

new.s: From where did the Harappans obtain tin?
new.x: Tin came from Afghanistan and Iran; copper from Khetri and gold from Kolar.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: tin -> Afghanistan, Iran

new.s: Which Harappan site is associated with salt production?
new.x: Salt was made at Kerala-no-dhoro; Kot Bala has the earliest furnace.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: salt -> Kerala-no-dhoro

new.s: At which Harappan site were workshops of ivory, copper and beads found?
new.x: Kuntasi on the Gujarat coast had ivory, copper and bead workshops.
new.angle: U0009 notes gap: Kuntasi workshops

new.s: Of which material was the measuring scale found at Lothal made?
new.x: Lothal yielded an ivory scale; the shell scale is from Mohenjodaro and the copper one from Harappa.
new.angle: U0010 notes gap: Lothal scale -> ivory

new.s: What was the smallest division on the ivory scale of Lothal?
new.x: The Lothal ivory scale has 27 divisions in about 46 mm, each about 1.70 mm.
new.angle: U0010 notes gap: Lothal scale unit 1.70 mm

new.s: Besides steatite, which material was also used for Harappan seals?
new.x: Seals were mostly of steatite, but also of terracotta, copper and ivory.
new.angle: U0010 notes gap: seal materials

new.s: How many Harappan characters are on the cylindrical steatite seal found at Rakhigarhi in June 2026?
new.x: The June 2026 Rakhigarhi seal has an alligator motif and five Harappan characters.
new.angle: U0010 notes gap: Rakhigarhi seal 2026 -> five characters

new.s: At which Mesopotamian site was an Indus seal with a unicorn and script found?
new.x: A Nippur seal carries the unicorn motif with Indus script.
new.angle: U0010 notes gap: Nippur unicorn seal

new.s: About how many inscribed Harappan objects are known?
new.x: The Indus script corpus has about 5,000 inscribed objects.
new.angle: U0010 notes gap: corpus ~5,000

new.s: At which Harappan site were circular pits with grave goods but no skeleton found?
new.x: Kalibangan has three burial types, one being circular pits with grave goods but no skeleton.
new.angle: U0011 notes gap: Kalibangan symbolic burials

new.s: Which of the following was NOT among Harappan toilet objects?
new.x: Bronze mirrors, ivory combs and collyrium sticks were used; iron was unknown.
new.angle: U0011 notes gap: cosmetics

new.s: Of which material is the Priest-King of Mohenjodaro made?
new.x: The Priest-King is a steatite bust; the Dancing Girl is bronze.
new.angle: U0012 notes gap: Priest-King -> steatite

new.s: For what were the perforated jars of the Harappans probably used?
new.x: Perforated jars, with a large hole at the base and small holes on the wall, were probably for straining liquor.
new.angle: U0012 notes gap: perforated jar -> straining liquor

new.s: Which was the most common type of Harappan pottery?
new.x: Plain red pottery was the most common; red pottery with black designs is the typical painted type.
new.angle: U0012 notes gap: plain red most common

new.s: In June 2026 NCERT decided to restore the original image of which Harappan sculpture in its new Class 9 Art textbook?
new.x: On 18 June 2026 NCERT said it would restore the original Dancing Girl image in the Class 9 Art textbook.
new.angle: U0012 notes gap: NCERT Dancing Girl 2026

new.s: The famous bronze Nataraja images of South India were cast by the lost-wax technique under which dynasty?
new.x: Chola bronzes such as the Shiva Nataraja were cast by the lost-wax (cire perdue) method.
new.angle: U0012 web: PYQ y358bc859520 lost-wax -> Nataraja (Chola bronzes)
